messages:
zayn: Strange one — our Vite edge sample app compiled fine but at runtime the worker crashes with `TypeError: Redwood.default.createClient is not a function`. Dev server (vite) works.

zayn: App import is `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference'` in TS. VSCode auto-import initially suggested `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` (default) in one file and we accidentally mixed both patterns.

ivy: I've seen this when tsc/TS server + editor auto-imports produce default imports while the package only provides named exports. When bundling, some toolchains wrap CJS/ESM interop and produce an object like `{ default: { createClient: [Function] } }` which trips edge runtimes that expect the ESM shape.

harry: Repro I used that always hits the error: 
1) create vite vanilla app + TS
2) import default in one module `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` and call `Redwood.createClient()`
3) import named in another file `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference'`
4) vite build, run in miniflare -> `Redwood.default.createClient is not a function` or sometimes `createClient is not a function` depending on optimizer.

ivy: Quick root cause: mix of editor auto-import + package only exporting named symbols. Vite/esbuild sometimes inserts `__toESM`/interop helpers that change the runtime shape, and TS auto-import chooses the default import if `esModuleInterop`/`allowSyntheticDefaultImports` is true in the app tsconfig.

eva: Short-term fixes: 
- Normalize imports in the app to named imports everywhere. Grep for `import Redwood` and replace with `import { createClient }`.
- Disable VSCode auto-fix or set TS server setting to prefer named imports.

eva: SDK-side mitigations we discussed: 
- Provide a default export in the ESM entry that mirrors the named exports (e.g. `export { createClient } from './dist/index.esm.js'; export default { createClient };`) so accidental default imports work.
- Or update README to add a note about preferred import style and TS settings (esModuleInterop implications).

harry: Another useful diagnostic: check the built chunk for `__toESM` or `__require` and open the runtime object printed in a worker log: `console.log(typeof Redwood, Object.keys(Redwood || {}))` to see whether the runtime sees the named function or a default wrapper.

zayn: Filed DX-9901 with a tiny repro (zip + exact tsconfig + vite config) and stack traces. editor-bot: Ticket DX-9901 created and linked.

ivy: Follow-up: SDK adding a permissive default export is low-risk and will make the SDK more friendly to mixed import styles in the wild. We should still recommend named imports in docs.

zayn: Thanks — I'll update the sample-apps to use named imports and add a CI lint that fails on `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` to catch accidental default imports.
